name: probelab
title: ProbeLab - 16-channel logic analyzer + 2-channel scope front-end (RP2040)
brief: ProbeLab: a USB-C logic analyzer for sigrok/PulseView (sigrok-pico class firmware). RP2040 with a 12 MHz crystal and a 16 MB W25Q128 QSPI flash, BOOTSEL and RESET buttons, USB-C with USBLC6 ESD, an AP2112K 3.3 V LDO (the RP2040 makes its own 1.1 V core). 16 logic inputs on two 2x10 0.1" headers (ground on every other pin), each clamped by a USBLC6-4SC6 and fed through 100R into one of two SN74LVC245A buffers that drive GPIO2-GPIO17. Two scope channels on a 1x4 header: AC/DC slide switch, 1M attenuator biased to mid-rail, TLV9061 buffer into the RP2040's own ADC (GPIO26/27). PWR, STAT and ACT LEDs, four M3 holes.

blocks.title: USB-C: 5 V in + USB 2.0 FS data

netClasses.name: PWR
netClasses.why: VBUS (receptacle, LDO, ESD and TVS rail pins: no fine-pitch pins) at 0.4 mm. 3V3 and 1V1 stay at the 0.2 mm default: they land on the RP2040's 0.2 mm QFN pins, and with neckdown off a 0.3 mm class left 6 power-pin connections open on 2026-09-30 until the ladder narrowed it. The board draws well under 150 mA; 0.2 mm carries about 0.5 A on an outer layer (IPC-2221, 10 C rise)

rules.why_clearance: the RP2040's QFN-56 pins are 0.2 mm wide on a 0.4 mm pitch, so 0.2 mm is pad-to-pad exactly; JLCPCB multilayer builds 0.09 mm spacing
rules.why_min_hole: the RP2040 QFN-56 ThermalVias footprint's own vias are 0.2 mm; JLCPCB multilayer boards drill 0.2 mm

keepouts.name: pin_labels_D10_D15
keepouts.why: via-free strip under the D10-D15 pin labels: the silk stage sets each label 1.65 mm inside its signal pad (x 7.19-9.80 for three characters) and never displaces a routed via; on 2026-10-01 router vias at (8.84, 40.29) and (9.53, 51.55) left D10 and D14 unlabelled on both faces. D0-D9 are two characters and end at x 9.04, clear of the vias the router puts beside the TVS pads

board.notes: 4 layers: F.Cu / In1 routing / In2 GND plane / B.Cu. The plane is on In2, not In1: measured 2026-09-30 on this placement, Freerouting 2.4.1 left every J2/J3 ground-pin connection open (23-30 opens, all GND, adjacent header pins included) whenever In1 was the Specctra power layer, and closed all of them with In2 as the power layer instead. In2 is a power layer during routing; every pour comes after a measured 0 open.

holes:H1?.why: M3 hole, top-left corner, 3.5 mm in from both edges

holes:H2?.why: M3 hole, top-right corner, 3.5 mm in from both edges

holes:H3?.why: M3 hole, bottom-left corner, 3.5 mm in from both edges

holes:H4?.why: M3 hole, bottom-right corner, 3.5 mm in from both edges: a symmetric 51 x 63 mm pattern on the 58 x 70 mm outline

bankA:J?.why: D0-D7 header on the left edge, pin 1 at the top; ground row outside, signal row inside; courtyard clears the corner hole

bankB:J?.why: D8-D15 header on the left edge below D0-D7, courtyards 0.1 mm apart

bankA:U2?.why: TVS for D0-D3 beside the header pins it clamps; its pads start 10.0 mm in, clear of the 3-character pin labels the silk stage sets 1.65 mm inside the signal pads

bankA:U3?.why: TVS for D4-D7, x as for D0-D3 so the front labels fit

bankA:U1?.why: D0-D7 buffer level with its header, A side facing it, B side facing the RP2040's GPIO2-9

bankB:U2?.why: TVS for D8-D11, x as for D0-D3 so the front labels fit

bankB:U3?.why: TVS for D12-D15, x as for D0-D3 so the front labels fit

bankB:U1?.why: D8-D15 buffer level with its header, B side facing the RP2040's GPIO10-17 corner

mcu:U?.why: RP2040 at the board's middle: GPIO2-17 face the buffers, QSPI/USB face up, ADC faces the scope channels

mcu:C1?.why: IOVDD pin 1 cap in the top-left corner pocket (GPIO0/1 beside it are unused), pad 1 toward the pin

mcu:C2?.why: IOVDD pin 10 cap level with its pin, pad 1 toward it; the GPIO lines on either side of pin 10 go round it

mcu:C12?.why: DVDD pin 50 (1V1) cap up and left of its pin; with the flash turned, no QSPI line has to cross this spot

mcu:C6?.why: IOVDD pin 49 cap straight above it, pad 1 also over USB_VDD pin 48 (both 3V3)

mcu:C7?.why: USB_VDD pin 48 cap up and right of its pin, as low as the USB lines beside it allow (pin 48 shares C6's pad 1 with pin 49)

mcu:C10?.why: VREG_VOUT (45) 1 uF up and right of its pin, leaving 1.05 mm between its pads and pin 48's cap for the USB lines (0.9 mm, the bare minimum for two, left U1_DM_MCU or VBUS open on 2026-10-01)

mcu:C9?.why: VREG_VIN (44) 1 uF right of pin 45's cap (pins 43 and 44 are both 3V3)

mcu:C8?.why: ADC_AVDD (43) 100 nF in the top-right corner, pad 1 toward the pin

mcu:C5?.why: IOVDD pin 42 cap level with its pin on the unused right side, pad 1 toward it

mcu:C4?.why: IOVDD pin 33 cap level with its pin, below the ADC/LED lines, pad 1 toward it

mcu:C3?.why: IOVDD pin 22 cap under its pin, right of the XOUT line

mcu:C11?.why: DVDD pin 23 (1V1) cap under the unused SWD pins 24/25, beside the pin 22 cap

mcu:Y?.why: crystal under XIN/XOUT, XIN pad top-left

mcu:R1?.why: 1k from XOUT down to the crystal's other pad, below the pin 22/23 caps

mcu:C13?.why: 15 pF on XIN, left of the crystal

mcu:C14?.why: 15 pF on the crystal's XOUT side, under it

mcu:R2?.why: 27R on D+ on the way up to the ESD clamp and receptacle

mcu:R4?.why: BOOTSEL 1k left of the flash, so only the slow BOOTSEL net runs to the button

mcu:R5?.why: RUN pull-up beside the RESET button

flash:U?.why: flash above the QSPI pins, turned so its SD0/SCLK/SD3 pads sit up and left of RP2040 pins 53/52/51 and its SS/SD1/SD2 pads face away from the RP2040: no QSPI line has to cross the space above pins 48-50, which their caps use

flash:C?.why: flash VCC cap beside its VCC pin (bottom right once turned)

usb:J?.why: receptacle on the top edge above the RP2040's USB pins, shell 0.6 mm proud

esd:U?.why: ESD clamp right under the receptacle, between it and the RP2040

ldo:U?.why: LDO beside the receptacle's VBUS pins

an_hdr:J?.why: scope header on the right edge, pin 1 (CH1) at the bottom beside CH1's front-end

scope2:SW?.why: CH2 AC/DC lever 0.85 mm proud of the right edge, above the scope header

scope1:SW?.why: CH1 AC/DC lever 0.85 mm proud of the right edge, below the scope header

scope2:C1?.why: CH2 coupling cap between the switch's input (pad 1) and common (pad 2) rows, clear of the DC and AC words the silk stage sets beside pads 1 and 3

scope1:C1?.why: CH1 coupling cap, placed as CH2's

scope2:U?.why: CH2 buffer between its switch and ADC1 (pin 39, the upper of the two)

scope1:U?.why: CH1 buffer between its switch and ADC0 (pin 38, the lower of the two)

boot:SW?.why: BOOTSEL on the top edge, near its 1k beside the flash

reset:SW?.why: RESET on the bottom edge, the side of the RP2040 its RUN pin is on

led_stat:R?.why: STAT LED on the bottom edge

led_act:R?.why: ACT LED on the bottom edge

route.why: the escalation ladder narrows only classes that carry an open net; the outline is stated, so it is never grown

switches.why: DC beside the throw that shorts the coupling capacitor, AC beside the open throw
DC beside the throw that shorts the coupling capacitor, AC beside the open throw

captions.place_3d: KiCad's raytracer on the placed board: two 2x10 probe headers on the left edge, USB-C on the top, the scope header and AC/DC switches on the right.
captions.done_3d: RP2040 + W25Q128, 16 buffered and clamped logic inputs, 2 scope channels into the RP2040 ADC, USB-C, BOOT/RST, PWR/STAT/ACT.
